cards.text: Zedekiah son of Josiah has just started his reign as king of Judah. Right at the beginning, the LORD gives a message to His prophet Jeremiah, and Jeremiah tells us about it himself. And friend, this message starts with an arts and crafts project.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Jeremiah to make out of leather straps and put on his neck?

cards.text: Envoys have come to Jerusalem to see King Zedekiah. They're from five nations: Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Sidon.

cards.question: Through these envoys from five nations, who does the LORD tell Jeremiah to send word to?

cards.text: And the message from the LORD of Hosts starts at the very beginning. By His great power and outstretched arm, He made the earth, and the people and animals on it.

cards.question: Since God made the earth, who does He say He gives it to?
So right now, whose authority does God place all these lands under?

cards.text: God calls him "My servant," and He even makes the beasts of the field subject to him. That man's chain of command goes all the way down to the field mice.
All nations will serve Nebuchadnezzar, and his son, and his grandson.

cards.question: True or false: God says Babylon will stay on top forever.

cards.text: Nope. When the time of his own land comes, many nations and great kings will enslave him. Even the biggest empire has a timer on it, and friend, I KNOW timers.

cards.question: True or false: God says any nation that won't serve Nebuchadnezzar will be punished by sword and famine and plague.
Jeremiah's leather yoke is a picture of the nations ___ the king of Babylon.

cards.text: Then comes a warning for those five kings. Don't listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dream interpreters, your mediums or your sorcerers.

cards.question: What are all those voices telling the five kings?

answers.text: You will not serve Babylon's king
Babylon's king will set you free
Your gods will fight for you

cards.question: God says those voices prophesy a ___ that will get the nations removed from their land.

cards.text: God says He'll banish them, and they'll perish. Those advisers are like a GPS that says "turn left" and points you straight into the lake.

cards.question: True or false: The nation that puts its neck under Babylon's yoke and serves him gets to stay in its own land.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah takes the same message to Zedekiah king of Judah. Same yoke, same neck, brand new audience.

cards.question: Jeremiah tells Zedekiah and his people to put their necks under Babylon's yoke, serve, and ___.

cards.text: Then he asks why Zedekiah and his people should die by sword, famine and plague. That's the prophet version of asking why we're doing this the HARD way.

cards.question: True or false: Jeremiah tells Zedekiah to listen to the prophets who say he must not serve the king of Babylon.
The LORD says He has not ___ the prophets telling Zedekiah not to serve Babylon.

cards.text: And yet they're prophesying falsely in His name. That's like a guy showing up at my bakery saying "Papa Dorin sent me," and I have NEVER seen this man in my life.

cards.question: What does God warn will happen to Zedekiah's people and those prophets together?

cards.text: Then Jeremiah turns to the priests and all the people. Their prophets have been saying something about the articles from the house of the LORD that are in Babylon.

cards.question: What are those prophets saying about the articles from the LORD's house?

answers.text: They'll be brought back very soon
They'll be melted down in Babylon
They'll be sold off to Egypt

cards.question: Jeremiah calls the prophets' claim a lie and says, "Serve the king of Babylon and live!" Then he asks why this city should become a ___.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah throws down a challenge. If they really are prophets and the word of the LORD is with them, let them plead with the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: If those prophets are the real thing, what should they plead with the LORD for?

answers.text: That the articles still left stay put
That the yoke on Judah breaks

cards.question: The pillars, the sea, the bases and the rest still in Jerusalem were left behind when Nebuchadnezzar carried a king of Judah into exile. Which one?
True or false: When Nebuchadnezzar carried Jeconiah off, he took all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem into exile too.
The LORD of Hosts says the articles still left in Jerusalem will be carried to ___.
True or false: God says the articles from His house will be lost in Babylon for good.

cards.text: They'll stay in Babylon until the day God attends to them again, and then He'll bring them back and restore them to this place. Not the prophets' day, friend. HIS day.
Hang onto that picture of Jeremiah in his leather yoke, friend. This story isn't done with us yet.

findings.problem: The question asks what happens to Zedekiah's people and the prophets together, and the right answer is 'They'll be banished and perish.' In Jeremiah 27:15 the LORD says 'I will banish you,' meaning Zedekiah and his people. Only the perishing is extended to 'you and the prophets who prophesy to you.' The text never says the prophets will be banished, so the answer isn't stated as true for both groups.

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both. When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'dream' is arguable. Card 14 lists 'dream interpreters' among the voices this question asks about, so a baker could argue that some of them prophesy a dream. Replace it with a word that can't be argued.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Babylon's king will set you free' means nearly the same as the right answer 'You will not serve Babylon's king.' Both say the nations won't stay in Babylon's service, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 18 is only the 'story isn't over' line. That is allowed because the last verse was asked on card 16. The card cites Jeremiah 27:22 but tells nothing from that verse, and its only image, Jeremiah in his leather yoke, comes from 27:2. The rule says to cite exactly what the card uses, but the docs don't say what a line-only closing card should cite.
findings.question: What should a closing story card that is only the 'story isn't over' line cite in its verses field: the passage's last verse, the verse of any image it mentions (here 27:2), or nothing?
